paper.title: POWERPLAY: Training an Increasingly General Problem Solver by Continually Searching for the Simplest Still Unsolvable Problem
paper.central_claim: PowerPlay searches pairs of new tasks and solver modifications until it finds a more powerful solver that provably solves all previously learned tasks plus the new one while its predecessor does not; by design it does not forget.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: subagent runtime exposes no receipt to the worker; model identity is the configured claude-kimi type only. Pure framework paper: no experiments in the pinned text; solver may be code (OOPS) or NN weights (Alg 4.3) so scope is boundary-in.

evidence.quote: a search algorithm is used to find a new pair that provably has the following properties:
evidence.support_explanation: States the acceptance criterion for a (task, solver-modification) pair: new task unsolved by predecessor, solved by successor, previous tasks still solved.

evidence.quote: The new task cannot be solved by the old problem solver.
evidence.support_explanation: Frontier condition: the invented task must lie outside the predecessor solver.

evidence.quote: The new solver can still solve the known set of previously learned tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Non-regression condition over the whole stored repertoire (the retention gate).

evidence.quote: provably (by design) does not have any problems with online learning
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim that the design cannot forget; this is a by-construction property, not a measured result.

evidence.quote: (often this replay-based test will actually be computationally cheaper than a test involving the environment)
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier for earlier tasks in partially observable/non-stationary environments is replay of recorded traces, not re-running the environment.

evidence.quote: will be saved in unmodifiable read-only storage,
evidence.support_explanation: Accepted p_i, s_i, T_i, Trace_i are persisted read-only and readable by later search programs.
Rejected candidate programs are rolled back (modifications of u and U undone) before the next candidate is tried; rollback is part of the method.

evidence.quote: provided the average performance on previously solved tasks does not decrease
evidence.support_explanation: Variant II relaxes strict non-regression to average-performance non-decrease, i.e. the gate is configurable.

evidence.quote: validity check does not require too much
evidence.support_explanation: Search is biased toward tasks whose validation touches few earlier tasks (component-to-task tracking L^k), the paper's answer to growing verification cost.

evidence.quote: This biases the search towards pairs that can be described compactly and validated quickly.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection rule: first found-and-validated pair under complexity-ordered (universal) search.

evidence.quote: did not have a built-in guarantee
evidence.support_explanation: Differentiator against the closest earlier system (the 1997-2002 left/right-brain curiosity systems): no built-in guarantee against forgetting.

evidence.quote: may potentially sacrifice large long-term gains for small short-term gains
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated failure boundary: greedy task choice may block harder tasks.

evidence.quote: First experiments are reported in separate papers
evidence.support_explanation: All empirical evidence is delegated to separate papers [53,52]; none is in the pinned material.
Acknowledges trivial tasks are initially admissible (modularization trap) and become inadmissible only after generalization; whether this limit is reached is not measured.

evidence.quote: should contain instructions for reading (and running) the code of the present problem solver
evidence.support_explanation: Search programs may read/run the current solver code, i.e. a self-referential option; only mentioned, not exercised.
One instantiation modifies RNN weight matrices (weight-level solver), the other (OOPS) modifies program code; scope is therefore boundary with respect to the non-weight rule.

evidence.quote: Standard problem solver architectures of personal computers or neural networks tend to generalize
evidence.support_explanation: Claim that continual task invention keeps breaking the solver's generalization; unsupported here (no measurement).

evidence.quote: Correctness demonstration may be the most time-consuming obligation
evidence.support_explanation: The commit check is the main cost and the paper only argues, without numbers, how to keep it bounded.
Searched Sections 1-11 of the pinned HTML (no appendix exists): no table, figure, benchmark, result number, baseline, seed, or cost measurement appears; Sec 8 defers to [53,52].

signatures.object: Pair (task T_i, solver s_i) appended to a growing repertoire; solver s_i is a program (OOPS/FORTH-like) or an RNN weight matrix; task set T_<=i is the stored repertoire.
signatures.information: Search program p may read solver code and recorded Trace history; tasks come with a deterministic solved-check J_i and resource bounds; no external labels or rewards in the basic variant.
signatures.operation: Search algorithm proposes candidate program p that (a) invents T, (b) modifies s_{i-1} into q, (c) runs Correctness Demonstration that q (not s_{i-1}) solves T and q still solves all earlier tasks.
signatures.output: Accepted tuple (i, p_i, s_i, T_i, Trace_i).
signatures.conditions: Deterministic tasks or replayable traces; solver architecture whose modifications can be checked; sufficient search time.
signatures.feedback: Internal: task checker J_i and replay of stored traces; no environment reward needed.
signatures.selection_rule: First candidate found under complexity-ordered universal search that passes the three-property test (strict non-regression + novelty); data = the stored task set itself.
signatures.persistence: Read-only storage of p_i, s_i, T_i, Trace_i; component-to-task lists L^k track which tasks depend on which solver components.
signatures.later_use: Later search programs may read/copy earlier programs and solutions (Alg 4.1); s_i is the base for step i+1.
signatures.claimed_effect: Continually growing repertoire without forgetting; verification cost need not grow with repertoire size (under modularity).
signatures.failure_boundary: Greedy (Sec 9.3), trivial-task modularization (Sec 5), noisy/non-stationary environments need trace replay or probabilistic variants (Sec 7.2), safety (Sec 10).

signatures.object: Variant II acceptance rule: explicit cost function over all tasks so far.
signatures.information: Same as S1 plus per-task time/space costs and a reward r_new for newly solved self-defined tasks.
signatures.operation: Accept s_i if Cost(s_{i-1},T_<=i) - Cost(s_i,T_<=i) > epsilon, allowing forgetting if overall cost improves.
signatures.conditions: Cost function with alpha trading space vs time; epsilon progress threshold.
signatures.feedback: Computed costs on the stored tasks.
signatures.selection_rule: Minimal savings epsilon across all tasks so far.
signatures.later_use: Val(s^k) per component can protect valuable components from being forgotten.
signatures.failure_boundary: No empirical test of the epsilon threshold in the pinned material.

gap.author_gap: Most CS automates solving given tasks; theoretically optimal universal solvers are impractical (constant slowdowns) and earlier curiosity systems could forget; need a practical way to keep inventing the simplest still-unsolved task while provably not losing earlier skills.
gap.checked_gap: Real and clearly stated: online curiosity-driven learners can forget (author asserts), and optimal solvers (Hsearch, Goedel machine) are impractical for small problems. The gap is stated at the level of design guarantees; its practical size is not measured in this paper.
lineage: Schmidhuber 1990-2002 curiosity/artificial-creativity systems incl. left/right-brain zero-sum game (cited [30,54,37,38]; versions not pinned)
Goedel machine / Hsearch / universal search / OOPS (cited [44,13,17,41])
gap.closest_adjacent: Previous left/right-brain curiosity system of the same author (no no-forgetting guarantee) and the Goedel machine (proof-gated self-rewrites, impractical constants).
gap.residue: Guarantee holds by construction only if the demonstration is exact; greedy choice, growing verification cost and reaching non-trivial generalization are open.
gap.stakes: Stated: ability to train increasingly general solvers without catastrophic forgetting; not quantified.
gap.method_response: Pair search over (task, solver modification) with a hard non-regression gate, trace replay, component-to-task tracking and cost-biased search order.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether this yields increasingly general solvers in practice (experiments deferred); verification cost under non-modular solvers; interaction with external tasks (Sec 6).
unresolved: Broader open-ended-learning / intrinsic-motivation neighbors beyond the author's own lineage (only [1,5,22,20] are named for comparison) are not analysed; no external versions pinned (separate papers [53,52] not in input pack).

rs_pattern.reason: Operation = system manufactures its own training tasks (no external labels) and passes every candidate through one explicit gate before it enters the repertoire, then iterates; closest RS main card is self_supervised_signal_engineering (generated-and-filtered samples) and sub C08 (generate beyond support, one gate, retrain, iterate). Fit is partial: the generator is a joint program search over (task, solver edit), the gate is an exact dominance check rather than a learned filter, and no real-target transfer step exists. Candidates read and rejected: reframe_as_solvable_object (reframing as pair search is real but there is no correspondence theorem beyond the induction sketch in 3.3.3), generative_process_redesign (not a generative procedure), assumption_audit_and_pivot (no audit/relaxation of a proof assumption).

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C08 step1 (binding constraint is the corpus) N/A: no corpus; step2 generator that reaches missing region: met in kind (task must be unsolvable by predecessor); step3 one load-bearing filter: met (Correctness Demonstration, Sec 2/3.3); step4 retrain on filtered set and iterate: met in kind (accept pair, repeat); step5 transfer to real target / cheaper baselines: not present in pinned material.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: explicit gate whose removal breaks the method - gate defined but not ablated (no experiments). Failure: unvalidated transfer to the real target - applies; omitted cheap baselines - applies.
matches.reason: Task invention is the manufactured signal; the demonstration is the single quality gate. Differs from siblings C07 (stability) and C26 (preference objective).

rs_pattern.executes_pattern: partial: generate-gate-iterate is specified algorithmically; nothing executed or measured in this paper.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: not_shown: no-forgetting is a design guarantee under exact demonstration; the problem of training increasingly general solvers is not shown closed.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS generate-gate-iterate over self-made training instances <-> domain proposer/solver pair with validity anchor: task invention + solver edit = proposal, Correctness Demonstration = validity/frontier check.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_or_differences: Domain H22 expects a learned (RL-trained) proposer rewarded at the solver frontier and a held-out certification; PowerPlay has search-based proposer, binary acceptance and no certification.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS single quality gate before folding into the corpus <-> domain commit rule authorising a change against an incumbent with rollback.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_or_differences: Gate here is deterministic non-regression, not a statistical commit rule; no disjoint validation split; verifier independence only partially met.

claims.text: The framework finds (task, solver) pairs such that the new solver solves all earlier tasks plus the new one while the predecessor does not; by design it cannot forget.
claims.setting: Abstract algorithmic framework; deterministic tasks or replayable traces.
claims.result_denominator: No empirical result; guarantee is by construction (induction sketch for prefix codes, Sec 3.3.3).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under an exact Correctness Demonstration the accept rule enforces strict non-regression on stored tasks; Variant II and probabilistic variants intentionally weaken this.

claims.text: Continual self-invented tasks train an increasingly general problem solver and keep breaking its generalization.
claims.result_denominator: None in this paper; deferred to [53,52].
claims.allowed_conclusion: No supported empirical statement from the pinned material.

claims.text: The cost of validating new tasks need not grow with repertoire size.
claims.setting: Modular solvers where components affect few tasks.
claims.result_denominator: Argued via L^k lists; no measurement.

assessment.evidence_level_note: No task/retained/improver evidence exists in the pinned paper (no experiments); the EVIDENCE scale starts at observed score gains.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A formally specified closed-loop self-modification scheme with an exact non-regression commit gate and read-only provenance, whose guarantee is by construction under exact demonstration.
unresolved: all empirical claims (generalization, repertoire growth, speed-up) deferred to separate papers not in the pack
scope: solver may be NN weights; non-weight program variant (OOPS) is the in-scope reading

G.reason: Gap is specific and sourced to the author's own lineage: earlier curiosity systems lacked a no-forgetting guarantee; optimal solvers impractical. Nearest neighbors compared are mostly self-citations; no broader curriculum/intrinsic-motivation comparison, so not 4.

M.reason: Mechanism is fully specified (invent, modify, demonstrate) and the reason it prevents forgetting is explicit and checkable; cost-biased search order explains why tasks stay simple. Assumptions (exact demonstration, greedy ok) are acknowledged but untested.

X.reason: Operation chain, gate, rollback, provenance and component tracking are reconstructable; Variant II shows the gate is configurable; failure boundaries are stated. Verifier independence and the concrete program language are only sketched.

E.measurement.reason: A verifier is defined by construction (task checker, trace replay) but no result is measured in the pinned paper, so verifier credibility is only potential.

E.causality.reason: No experiment, ablation or baseline in the pinned material; experiments are deferred to separate papers.
